title: chant-health/v1
description: What `chant lifecycle health <env> --json` prints (#4177): whether each declared resource that has a health read is up, read separately from drift. Every entity a read applies to lands in exactly one of `entities` (read, with a state), `unobserved` (the read failed, never folded into unhealthy) or `absent` (the provider says it is not deployed). Entity names are the graph's node ids. A single-stack project puts `lexicons` at the top level; a multi-stack one nests them under `stacks`. Written by the first chant release after 0.124.32. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version.

chantVersion.description: The chant that ran the read.

environment.description: The environment named on the command line.

observedAt.description: When the command started reading, ISO 8601 UTC.

summary.description: Counts over every lexicon and stack.

stacks.description: Per stack name, the same per-lexicon results.

byLexicon.description: Per lexicon name, that lexicon's read. A lexicon with no applicable entity is left out.

absent.description: Entity names the provider says are not deployed.

state.description: healthy and unhealthy are what the provider reported. unknown means the read succeeded and the answer decides neither way: a rollout in progress, a service scaled to zero, a condition pending.

detail.description: One short line saying why, in the provider's terms.

checkedAt.description: When the provider last checked or changed the state, when it says, ISO 8601.

hole.description: A read that failed. Never counted as unhealthy.

queried.description: The address the read was issued against, when the lexicon reports it.
